fixed.red: Unchanged code (origin/main 6036184). The test sets enterich.erpnext.CALL_TIMEOUT to 0.2 and erp.slow[COMMENT_METHOD] to 0.5, and keeps the 60 s OPERATION_TIMEOUT, so the comment call hits its own limit while the operation still has time left. Command: uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py -k too_late. It failed on `assert result["warnings"] == ["Enterich's comment may be missing from the draft: ERPNext didn't answer within 0.2 seconds."]`, because the result held "Enterich's comment couldn't be added to the draft: ERPNext didn't answer within 0.2 seconds.". The test also checks that the fake ERPNext received the comment's POST for the new draft. After the fix it passes, and the full suite passes (1580 tests).
fixed.notes: The branch did not exist yet, so I built it from origin/main. The fix is in _comment in src/enterich/tools/__init__.py. A Refused answer still says the comment "couldn't be added". Any other ErpnextError now says "may be missing from the draft", because the POST had already gone out: a timeout, a transport error, a redirect, an answer that isn't JSON or one that is too large. I checked the other places that handle a failure after a write: the creates of the draft writes in order_to_cash, procure_to_pay, record_to_report and bank_and_cash already say "the first may have been saved", and the deadline path of _comment already said "may be missing". So _comment was the only place this cause reached. CHANGELOG.md has a line under Unreleased / Fixed. ruff check, ruff format --check, basedpyright and mdformat --check all pass.

review.reason: Red/green redone in a detached worktree: at d6371fd5 (test:) the test tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py::test_a_comment_erpnext_answers_too_late_may_be_missing fails (1 failed, 5 comment tests passed); at c88c1ef9 (fix:) it and tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py plus tests/unit/test_tools.py pass (134 passed). The test asserts through the tool result a caller sees: the draft exists, the fake received the comment POST for that draft, and the warning's full text says "may be missing" with CALL_TIMEOUT 0.2 below the time left in the 60 s operation, which is exactly the finding's scenario. It doesn't repeat an existing test: the existing ones at :620, :761 and :833 check only `"comment" in missing`. It sits next to test_the_comment_stays_within_the_operation_time and uses the same fixtures and style. The fix (src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:144-149) keeps "couldn't be added" for Refused (already imported at :31) and words every other ErpnextError as "may be missing", which matches the existing deadline path at :150-155. It fits REQ-001-PRS-F015 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:401), and CHANGELOG.md has a line under Unreleased/Fixed. No docs or tests pinned the old wording. Where else the mechanism runs: _comment has one caller (_attempt, :345), which serves both creates and updates. I probed other paths with throwaway tests that went away with the worktree. A 403 refusal still says "couldn't be added ... ERPNext refused". A 302 redirect now says "may be missing". A late comment answer on update_draft_sales_invoice also says "may be missing". Write failures after the POST/PUT go through _written ("ERPNext saved the draft...") or the create descriptions' "the first may have been saved", as the notes say. One small point: a transport error raised before anything was sent now gets the hedged "may be missing" too. That wording is still true, and the notes name it. No change outside the finding. The repository is unchanged and the worktree is removed.

commits: 8a8786fba1bb50b4d68c41ed51035595181970ba test: a key without alg is refused for an algorithm of another key type
9393181286968d743403d3a9a1af9116b6b25b68 fix: refuse a token for a key of another type than its algorithm
fixed.red: I ran `uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_auth.py -k another_key_type` on unchanged origin/main (6036184), and all 4 cases failed. In each case the JWKS publishes a key without `alg`, settings use RS256,ES256, and the token's kid names that key. [EC key, RS256] and [RSA key, ES256] raised `TypeError: Expecting a PEM-formatted key.` from jwt/algorithms.py (:538 and :735) through Verifier._verify's jwt.decode. [oct key, ES256] raised `ValueError: Unable to load PEM file`. In all three, verify_token set no refusal and the app answered 500. [oct key, RS256] was refused, but the assertion `refusal(...) == "algorithm not the key's"` failed because the reason was "invalid token". After the fix all 81 tests in test_auth.py pass. The full gate also passes: pytest without e2e (1583 passed), ruff check, ruff format --check, basedpyright with 0 errors, and mdformat --check.
fixed.notes: The fix is in src/enterich/auth.py, Verifier._verify. After the `key.alg` check and before decoding, it calls `jwt.get_algorithm_by_name(alg).prepare_key(key.key)`. If that raises jwt.PyJWTError, TypeError or ValueError, the token is refused as "algorithm not the key's". This covers every key type the loader keeps without `alg`: RSA, EC, oct, and an EC key on another curve (InvalidKeyError, which used to give "invalid token"). It also covers both PyJWT error types, TypeError and ValueError. Verifier._verify is the only place that decodes a token, so there is no other caller to close. CHANGELOG.md has a line under Unreleased > Fixed. Left out: the finding also proposed an app-level test that the same token gets a 401 and a `rejection` line. That test would go in an integration test file such as tests/integration/test_auth*.py, which is not this branch's file. Turning a set refusal into a 401 with a `rejection` line is shared app behaviour that is already covered for the other refusal reasons.

review.reason:
I accept the fix. I redid the red check in a detached worktree. At 8a8786f (test:), all 4 cases of tests/unit/test_auth.py::test_a_key_without_alg_is_refused_for_an_algorithm_of_another_key_type failed. At 9393181 (fix:), all 81 tests in test_auth.py passed, and ruff check, ruff format --check and basedpyright found nothing in the two changed files.

The test: it sits next to the existing alg-member test (test_auth.py:187) and does not repeat it, because that test covers a key that names its alg. It asserts the refusal reason "algorithm not the key's" through verify_token/last_refusal, which is the claim the finding says is missing.

The fix: src/enterich/auth.py:181-186 in Verifier._verify calls jwt.get_algorithm_by_name(alg).prepare_key(key.key) before jwt.decode. It runs whether or not the key names an alg, so a curve mismatch on a key that does name one is caught too. It turns PyJWTError, TypeError and ValueError into _Refused("algorithm not the key's"). It stays within REQ-002-PRS-NF001: a wrong key gets a 401. CHANGELOG.md has a line under Unreleased > Fixed. Nothing else changed.

Other places the mechanism runs: a grep of src/ found no other jwt.decode or prepare_key, so _verify is the only decode path. I also tried every kind of key the loader keeps (RSA 2048 and 1024, EC P-256/P-384/P-521/secp256k1, Ed25519, oct; Ed448 is dropped by the loader) against all 10 ALLOWED_ALGORITHMS in config.py:20, using PyJWT 2.15.1. Every mismatch is now refused by prepare_key. Every match reaches decode and fails only with PyJWTError subclasses, which are already turned into refusals. The one other outcome was InsecureKeyLengthWarning for a 1024-bit RSA key, and that is a warning, not an exception, in normal running.

The notes name what was left out, the app-level test for a 401 with a `rejection` line, and the reason. The worktree is removed and the repository was not changed.

fixed.red: On the unchanged code (origin/main 6036184), `uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_config.py` gave 3 failures. The two new ISSUER rows got ['ENTERICH_RESOURCE_URL: must be a URL the metadata can publish'] where the test expected ['ENTERICH_ISSUER: must be a URL the metadata can publish']. When both RESOURCE_URL and ISSUER were bad, test_each_url_the_metadata_cannot_publish_is_named failed because the right side had one more item: the ENTERICH_ISSUER problem was missing. After the fix all 1582 tests pass (e2e excluded), and ruff check, ruff format --check, basedpyright and mdformat --check are clean.
fixed.notes: Fix in src/enterich/config.py `_Reader.as_published`: it reads the failing fields from `ValidationError.errors()` (issuer_url maps to ISSUER, resource_server_url to RESOURCE_URL) and names each one that failed. If no known field is named, it falls back to RESOURCE_URL as before, so a failure is never dropped silently. There is a CHANGELOG line under Unreleased/Fixed. The branch did not exist before, so it was created from origin/main. Not changed, because it is outside this finding: `_valid_host` still accepts all-digit hosts like 999.0.0.1 for JWKS_URL and ERPNEXT_URL, which never pass through the SDK check. No published metadata depends on them, so the finding's cause (blaming the wrong variable) does not reach them.

problems: src/enterich/config.py:135-136 (load), another path of the same mechanism: `reader.as_published` runs only `if resource and issuer`, so the SDK check is the only thing that catches an all-digit host like 999.x, and it is skipped for one URL whenever the other fails `_Reader.url`. I tried it on 5a41c811. ENTERICH_ISSUER=https://999.0.0.1/r with ENTERICH_RESOURCE_URL=ftp://x gives only ['ENTERICH_RESOURCE_URL: must be an http or https URL with a valid host']. RESOURCE_URL=https://999.1.1.1/mcp with ISSUER='' gives only ['ENTERICH_ISSUER: required'], and with ISSUER=http://id.example.com/x it gives only the https rule. In each case the second invalid variable is not named, which goes against REQ-002-PRS-NF005 (every invalid variable named), the requirement the finding cites. The fix and its tests leave this open, and the report's notes don't name it. They name only JWKS_URL and ERPNEXT_URL, which never pass through the SDK. Possible fix: check each URL that passed on its own (for example a per-field AnyHttpUrl/TypeAdapter under the SDK's config), so neither waits on the other.
review.reason: I read the finding record at 25dd758 and the commits aef152d3 (test) and 5a41c811 (fix). In a scratch worktree the new tests failed at aef152d3: 3 failed, 106 passed in tests/unit/test_config.py, the failures matching the report. At 5a41c811 all 109 pass. The tests check the problem list a caller sees through load(), as the neighbouring rows of test_invalid_values_stop_enterich_with_name_and_rule do. They sit next to those rows and don't repeat an existing test. The fix reads the failing fields from ValidationError.errors() loc (issuer_url / resource_server_url) and falls back to RESOURCE_URL. It stays within REQ-002-PRS-NF005 and has a CHANGELOG line under Fixed. Nothing beyond the finding changed. Other inputs of the same kind work: xn--a hosts are named correctly for both ISSUER and RESOURCE_URL, and a bare host, a percent-encoded path and a trailing slash are accepted. But load() at src/enterich/config.py:135-136 calls as_published only when both URLs passed _Reader.url. So a 999.x host in one URL goes unreported whenever the other URL is invalid (reproduced, see problems). The finding's cause, a bad URL never named, still reaches that path, and the notes don't mention it. I removed the worktree, and the repository is unchanged.
